heroSummary: The Bambu Lab P1P prints Overture Rock PLA reliably up to 190 mm/s capped at a 16 mm³/s volumetric flow limit. However, because the mineral rock speckles are abrasive, you must upgrade the stock stainless steel nozzle to a hardened steel assembly to prevent rapid bore wear.
bedSurfaceRecommendation: Textured PEI Plate (no adhesive required; clean with dish soap and warm water)
slicerTweaks: Set Max Volumetric Speed to 16 mm³/s in the filament profile to prevent under-extrusion at high P1P print speeds.
Set Printing Temperature to 208°C for all layers, with Initial Layer Bed Temperature at 55°C and Other Layers at 55°C.
Calibrate Pressure Advance to approximately 0.024-0.028 to maintain crisp corners despite the composite mineral content.
Enable Scarf Joint Seams and set outer wall speed to 120 mm/s to ensure consistent matte surface sheen and hide layer starts.

troubleshootingMatrix.issue: Progressive over-extrusion, layer roughness, and loss of dimensional accuracy over multiple prints
troubleshootingMatrix.rootCause: The mineral additives in Rock PLA rapidly eroded the stock stainless steel nozzle orifice, enlarging the bore diameter.
troubleshootingMatrix.exactFix: Install a Bambu Lab 0.4mm Hardened Steel complete hotend assembly and recalibrate extrusion width.

troubleshootingMatrix.issue: Intermittent nozzle clogs or extruder grinding during fast infill transitions
troubleshootingMatrix.rootCause: Exceeding the melt rate capacity of the mineral-filled polymer blend beyond 16 mm³/s.
troubleshootingMatrix.exactFix: Cap the Maximum Volumetric Speed to 15-16 mm³/s in OrcaSlicer and raise nozzle temperature from 208°C to 215°C.

troubleshootingMatrix.issue: Uneven gloss bands and shiny rings along outer perimeters
troubleshootingMatrix.rootCause: Speed and thermal fluctuation causing matte PLA surface microtexture variations between slow outer perimeters and fast infill.
troubleshootingMatrix.exactFix: Unify outer and inner wall speeds to a fixed 120 mm/s and maintain part cooling fan speed consistently at 90-100%.

faq.question: Can I print Overture Rock PLA with the stock P1P stainless steel nozzle?
faq.answer: While it will extrude initially, the mineral flecks are abrasive and will noticeably degrade the stainless steel nozzle within a few hundred grams. Upgrading to a hardened steel hotend is strongly recommended.

faq.question: Do I need to enclose the Bambu Lab P1P to print Overture Rock PLA?
faq.answer: No. Rock PLA is a modified PLA base material and prints optimally in open-air environments; closing the chamber can cause heat creep and clogging.

faq.question: Is Overture Rock PLA safe to use with the Bambu AMS unit?
faq.answer: Yes, but prolonged use of abrasive filaments can slowly wear down the standard AMS funnel guide tubes; consider fitting printed wear protectors or hardened funnel inserts.

faq.question: Why does my print look glossy instead of matte stone?
faq.answer: Printing too slowly or at temperatures above 215°C can burn off the matte finish; ensure your part cooling fan is above 80% and print at 208°C with consistent wall speeds.
